title: Todo lo que había pasado antes
blurbEn: Running into the teacher who taught her first six months, and everything that had changed since.
body:
Ayer volví a ver a la profesora que me enseñó español el primer año.

Se había jubilado en septiembre y no habíamos vuelto a hablar desde entonces.

La reconocí enseguida, aunque llevaba el pelo más corto. Ella tardó un poco más. Me sorprendió lo pequeña que parecía fuera del aula.

—Ana —dijo al final—. La que nunca hablaba en clase.

Era verdad. Durante seis meses no había abierto la boca más de tres veces. Había hecho todos los deberes, había aprobado todos los exámenes y no había dicho una sola frase completa en voz alta.

Ayer estuvimos veinte minutos hablando en español en mitad de la calle.

Le di las gracias con torpeza y ella hizo un gesto con la mano.

—Sabía que hablarías. Todos hablan al final. Solo hay que esperar.

Habrá dicho lo mismo a cien alumnos. No me importa.
translationEn:
Yesterday I ran into the teacher who taught me Spanish in my first year.

She had retired in September and we hadn't spoken since.

I recognised her immediately, although her hair was shorter. She took a little longer. I was surprised by how small she seemed outside the classroom.

"Ana," she said finally. "The one who never spoke in class."

It was true. For six months I hadn't opened my mouth more than three times. I had done all the homework, I had passed all the exams and I had not said a single complete sentence out loud.

Yesterday we spent twenty minutes talking in Spanish in the middle of the street.

I thanked her clumsily and she made a gesture with her hand.

"I knew you'd speak. They all speak in the end. You just have to wait."

She'll have said the same thing to a hundred students. I don't care.

Se había jubilado.note: Before the meeting, so one step further back than 'volví a ver'.

hablarías.note: The plain conditional, used here for the future seen from a point in the past: I knew, back then, that you would.

Habrá dicho.note: Guessing again, not future: she has probably said it many times.

phrases.note: 'volver a' + verb means to do something again.

phrases.gloss: in the middle of the street
